{"metadata":{"description":"DeepSeek Harness dynamic plugin: QR-code sidebar button for connecting mobile devices to the web UI","id":"gh:1334092636","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-plugin-qr-connect","slug":"mervyn-teo/dsh-plugin-qr-connect","topics":["cordis","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","mobile","pairing","qr-code","reverse-proxy"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"DeepSeek Harness dynamic plugin: QR-code sidebar button for connecting mobile devices to the web UI"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-plugin-qr-connect"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web
plugin that adds a **QR-code button above the Settings button** in the "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"sidebar
footer. It runs a small auth-gated reverse proxy so a phone on the same network
(or the inte"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"rnet) can scan a QR code and open the web UI securely. It is a
persistent bundle plugin (a host half"},{"id":"p4s4","text":" plus a browser half) that loads on every
boot."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Demo"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## What it does"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- Adds a full-width button (`sidebar.footer.action`, id `qr-connect`) stacked
**above** the shipped "},{"id":"p7s2","text":"Plugins button.
- Opens a fading panel with **two** QR codes:
- **Local network** — `http://<lan-ip>"},{"id":"p7s3","text":":<port>/?auth=<secret>`.
- **Public internet** — `http://<public-ip>:<port>/?auth=<secret>` (blue).
"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"- The reverse proxy (a child `node` process on `0.0.0.0:<port>`) validates the
secret, issues a sess"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"ion cookie (default 30 days), and forwards to the
loopback web UI — including WebSocket upgrades so "},{"id":"p7s6","text":"live updates reach the phone.
- The secret rotates every 30s by default and the QR refreshes to matc"},{"id":"p7s7","text":"h
(configurable; `0` disables auto-refresh).
- Click a QR to copy its link; the public QR has an inf"},{"id":"p7s8","text":"o tooltip.
- A **QR connect** card under Settings → Plugins configures the proxy port,
session lengt"},{"id":"p7s9","text":"h, and refresh interval.
- English and Chinese UI via DSH's locale service."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Files"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"| File | Purpose |"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"| `lib/index.js` | Host half — runs the reverse proxy and the `/__qr/*` state routes. |
| `lib/clien"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"t.js` | Browser half — the QR button and the settings card. |
| `lib/proxy.cjs` | The auth-gated rev"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"erse proxy child process (HTTP + WebSocket). |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Composition patch that inserts"},{"id":"p10s4","text":" the plugin row. |
| `package.json` | Package metadata (`dsh.bundle` + `dsh.client` manifest). |"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"Then restart `dsh web` — host bundles load at boot."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"Defaults live in `cordis.patch.yml` (`port`, `sessionDays`, `refreshSeconds`,
`publicHost`). Change "},{"id":"p14s2","text":"them there (or in the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`)
and restart, or adjust them from the setting"},{"id":"p14s3","text":"s card — edits are written to the
`qr-connect` settings namespace's user layer, so they survive rest"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"arts and
layer over the composition defaults. `publicHost` is a custom domain or IP
used for the pub"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"lic-internet QR code instead of the auto-detected public IP
(accepts `host`, `host:port`, or a full "},{"id":"p14s6","text":"`https://` origin; empty = auto-detect). The host half serves three same-origin routes the
browser h"},{"id":"p14s7","text":"alf uses: `GET /__qr/info`, `POST /__qr/rotate`, and
`GET|POST /__qr/config`."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- DSH with the `subprocess`, `fs`, and `webServer` services mounted, plus the
`settings` service for"},{"id":"p16s2","text":" the Settings → Plugins card (without it the card is
hidden and edits stay runtime-only).
- Internet"},{"id":"p16s3","text":" access from the DSH host for the public-IP lookup
(`https://api.ipify.org`).
- The scanning device "},{"id":"p16s4","text":"must be able to reach the proxy port (a host firewall may
need an allow rule); the public QR also ne"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"eds internet reachability
(port-forwarding)."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"Local-IP and public-IP detection run in-process (no `ip`/`curl`/shell commands),
and manual secret r"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"otation signals the proxy child over its stdin, so the host
half works on Windows, macOS, and Linux."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"## Security"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"The proxy exposes the full agent shell to anyone who can reach the port, gated
only by the 30s secre"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"t and the session cookie. Use a short session length and
treat this as a trusted-network convenience"},{"id":"p19s3","text":", not a hardened remote-access layer."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## License"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"MIT"}],"truncated":false}
